text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cultists leave wake of sadness, questions: Some relatives of suicide victims say they expected tragedy.
- Sex, sleaze tales add to miseries of British PM: Trailing far behind Labour in polls, Major hardly needs 'terrible chaos'
- Axworthy to press China on rights: Environment, non-trade issues on agenda that aims to 'refocus' relations.
- Bre-X's president just one of the guys: Buddies stand behind David Walsh.
- Nightmaare of Davis Inlet haunting Innu dreams: Visions of life in Sango Bay dance in heads of Davis Inlet's people as they sit in the wreckage of the past.
- Bre-X assay mystery deepens: Company supplied Barrick with hundreds of ore samples for independent testing.
- The squeeze is on baseball: Three years after a paralyzing strke, the sport is making a pitch to win back fans and sponsors and boost teams' fortunes. It will require a grand-slam effort.
- OSC reins in fund dealers: Given one year to self-regulate.
- Outlook turns gloomier for stocks, bonds.
- Bre-X fallout puts heat on regulators: Analysts warn Canadian junior miners will all pay penalty for Busang disaster. Far-reaching investigations likely.
- Rate jitters, Bre-X woes a lethal mix for the TSE.
